Garo Dictionaries have contributed a great deal to enrich Garo litera- ture But of all dictonaries conected with Garo literature, the Bengali- Garo dictionary produced by Rev Ramke W Momin in 1887 in Bengali character, whch contains more than 35,000 words, will perhaps be the first and the most exhaustive literary work in tnbal languages of the North East and, besides, his ingenious and scholarly bent of mind, it reflects his total mastery ot Bengali and Garo languages Miss Linne M Holbrook, a lady Missionary of great repute, also occupies a unique place in the literary world of the Garo as one of the major contnbutors for the enrichment of Garo literature Appointed by the Women's Bapust Foreign Mission Society on Apnl 9, 19(06 to work parucularly tor Garo women, she came to Garo Hills and reached Tura stories in six volumes, fables, histories, doctnnes, besides editing and lated by others.

--- Page 10 --- (m) One of the most monumental works and probably one of the best coritrbuiuons to Garo literature by a Missionary, leave alone the Garos, will be the manuscripts prepared by Miss Holbrook for Garo-English dictionary To collect more than 14,000 Garo words, the work for which began with the collection of the Garo word "Chu" or "Water" in 1906 itself, took her more than 30 long years Miss Holbrook, who undertook this most novel literary venture, took the manuscripts along with her to the Unuted States of America when she finally leit for home in March 1940 For about six years she worked on the manuscripts to put it into hook form, particularly, such painlsaking and laborious works as arranging the manuscripts in alpha- this work demanded ot her the expertuse and ingenuity of a scholar and total mastery of the language Having completed the manuscripts in 1946, though not free from shortcomings and literary flaws, she sent it to Tura for corection and printing But no record was found as through long years this treasure house of Garo vocabulary lay almost untouched ary stalwarts among the Garos to review the manuscripts and give it to Tura Book Room for publication But nothing came of it Finally the Garo Literature Society ventured to undertake this work, wherein our forefathers had fauled, by publishing the manuscripts ler attempt of the Society also failed due to certain unavoidable cir- cumstances and, thus, it took more than ten years to translate the dream of the Society into reality by publshing thus most precious manuscript As the General Secretary of the Garo Literature Society, I take ture Department, Government of Meghalaya, for extending financial assistance to the Garo Literature Society to publish this work.
